question: G0's target of 180 two-band regions was not met at 161. Is that a limit of DP2, or of how these 200 tracts were chosen?
finding: Band availability in the unselected pool is 87%, statistically identical to the 86.5% in the chosen 200. The selection was not unlucky; it is representative. But the distribution is lopsided rather than uniform -- most tracts carry five or six bands and a minority carry one -- so the shortfall is not scarcity, it is that the selection never filtered on band count. A SIA query answers that per tract before any pixels are fetched.

projection.note: 200 x 1.00 availability x 0.931 fetchability = 186, which clears the 180 target. The fetchability factor is measured, not assumed: 12 of 173 available second bands returned all-NaN pixels at our positions.

cost: Reselecting tracts invalidates every downstream comparison. G1 through G9 are all measured on these 200 regions, and this session verified nine of their figures against raw inputs. A new selection means re-acquiring roughly 14 GB, re-running reconcile, recovery and the anomaly scan, and re-verifying everything -- to raise one count from 161 to about 186.
recommendation: Not worth doing to satisfy a count. Worth doing if the science wants deeper multi-band coverage for its own sake, in which case filter on measured band availability at the selection step rather than after acquisition.
reproduce: see section 48; the sample is a deterministic stride over the unselected pool
